propositions: The ADR-promised byte-total backstop trigger in _gc_pass was never implemented; it reads only free disk space and mtime, never consulting _cache.byte_total, leaving the store with no size-based reclamation mechanism.

materialize_tickets bypasses cache.acquire entirely and never calls add_bytes, so tickets entries (~620 MiB each and the dominant consumer) contribute zero to the incremental byte total, causing severe under-counting.

The missing byte-total trigger and missing byte accounting for tickets entries are independent gaps that both contributed to disk pressure breaching 85–90% on the review-bot host with no reclamation firing.

A new configurable max_bytes cap with a default of zero (off) drives LRU-by-mtime eviction down to a target margin when armed, and materialize_tickets now accounts its entries via add_bytes on the populate-race win branch.
